You Can Actually Buy Tony Stark’s Custom Acura NSX From “The Avengers”
15 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Not only you can now buy Tony Stark’s ride from Marvel’s “The Avengers,” but you will also get a few extra goodies if you do. And if you must know, the vehicle is offered at the excitement of no reserve, meaning that it will change hands at the end of the ongoing online auction regardless of the highest bid.
Mind you, it’s not exactly a new-age machine, as you already know, as the custom Acura NSX Roadster Concept is actually based on a 1991 Acura NSX . Thus, despite the quite modern look, it builds on the original NSX. And it wasn’t a barely-driven example either, as it had accumulated more than 252,000 miles (~405,500 km) before it was converted to a movie prop. At the time of cataloging, the original odometer read 252,200 miles (~405,900 km).
This Acura NSX Roadster Concept is finished in Hot Rod Red on top of a black interior, and is currently located in Torrance, California. It was built by Trans FX for the movie, according to the seller, which is Acura, and after its premiere on the big screen, it was preserved by the automaker. Subsequently, the car returned to public display as part of the NSX’s 35th anniversary celebration, and now it is offered for sale, so you can own this piece of automotive and movie history.
The seller says that the machine features no hardtop, and compares it to the original Dodge Viper by stating that it has no roof and no windows. Acura also says that there is a VIN and a Carfax history report, though these are not shared in the ad. The vehicle is being sold “as a non-registerable manufacturer prototype,” and therefore “cannot be titled or registered for public road use.”
Photo: Cars&Bids Thus, you cannot legally drive it on public roads, so it is basically a show and tell kind of ride, albeit one that is definitely a conversation starter. So, it is up to you to decide whether it is worth your hard-earned money, though it would definitely make for a great addition to a collection, as it is something else entirely, not to mention one of a kind.
Some of the features mentioned in the listing include the custom bodywork , which was made of resin and fiberglass, as well as the custom paint finish that matches Iron Man’s armor. The “STARK 33” license plate that was used in the movie is also on deck, as you can see in the pictured shared above, and it accompanies the car. Other gizmos include the sports seats, which are aftermarket, and the 18-inch wheels at the front and 20-inch wheels at the rear.
But what about the known flaws? Well, other than the fact that you cannot drive this one-of-a-kind Acura NSX Roadster on public roads, the listing also reveals that the custom bodywork is fragile. Moreover, there are some micro scratches on the A pillars, doors, and front and rear bumpers, and some paint cracks on the C pillars. The door cards, left kick panel and right A pillar trim have scuffs on them, and the left door armrest is said to be warping.
Photo: Cars&Bids The firepower is supplied by a 3.0-liter VTEC V6 engine. The DOHC 24-valve mill was good for roughly 270 horsepower when the car was new, and 210 pound-feet (285 Nm) of torque, so it clearly won’t break any speed records. In fact, this machine looks a lot faster than it actually is, but then again, you are looking at the stock power of the first-gen Acura NSX . Everything is channeled to the rear wheels through a five-speed manual transmission. Thus, you also must know how to drive stick if you plan on moving it in your garage.
There are no detailed service entries mentioned in the ad, and the one-off machine is accompanied by one key, two key fobs, a certificate of authenticity, and a signed photo of the Acura Creative Director with the NSX, the listing reveals.
This Acura NSX Roadster Concept is advertised as part of an ongoing online auction on Cars&Bids, and you have ten days left to decide whether it is worth your money or not. That’s because the gavel will hit the table next Saturday, on October 31. The machine is advertised at the excitement of no reserve, as mentioned above, and at the time of writing, the highest bid was already at $80,497.
With ten days left until the event ends, there is plenty of time for this car to venture into the six-digit territory. By comparison, a first-gen Acura NSX typically sells for between $70,000 and over $170,000, and can reach a quarter of a million bucks for low-mileage examples that are in great shape overall. So, how much do you think this movie prop is actually worth? Interested parties can check it out in more detail here.
